[[File:BrindAmour_2009-01-06_1562v1_wiki.jpg|thumb|right|Current Head Coach Rod Brind'Amour as captain of the Carolina Hurricanes in 2009]]

The [[Carolina Hurricanes]] are an American professional [[ice hockey]] team based in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. They play in the [[Metropolitan Division]] of the [[Eastern Conference (NHL)|Eastern Conference]] in the [[National Hockey League]] (NHL).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311030113/http://www.nhl.com/ice/teams.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 11, 2009|title=Teams|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-24}}</ref> The current head coach is [[Rod Brind'Amour]]. The team joined the NHL in 1979 as an [[expansion team]] as the [[Hartford Whalers]], but moved to Raleigh, North Carolina in 1997. The Hurricanes won their first [[Stanley Cup]] [[List of Stanley Cup champions|championship]] in 2006.<ref name="history">{{cite web|url=http://hurricanes.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=2738|title=Franchise Timeline|publisher=Lincoln Hockey and the National Hockey League|work=NHL.com|accessdate=2008-12-24|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20090308133751/http://hurricanes.nhl.com/team/app/?service=page&page=NHLPage&id=2738|archivedate=2009-03-08}}</ref> Having first played at the [[Greensboro Coliseum]], the Hurricanes have played their home games at the [[PNC Arena]], which was first named the Raleigh Entertainment & Sports Arena, since 1999.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rbccenter.com/default.asp?RBCcenter=88&urlkeyword=Arena_Info|title=Arena Info|publisher=[[RBC Center]]|accessdate=2008-12-24|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222091507/http://www.rbccenter.com/default.asp?RBCcenter=88&urlkeyword=Arena_Info|archivedate=2008-12-22}}</ref> The Hurricanes are owned by [[Thomas Dundon|Tom Dundon]] and [[Eric Tulsky]] is their [[general manager]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/team/staff|title=Staff Directory|website=Carolina Hurricanes|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-07}}</ref>

There have been five&nbsp;[[head coach]]es for the Hurricanes team. The team's first head coach was [[Paul Maurice]], who has coached for six seasons. Maurice is the team's all-time leader for the most games coached, game wins and [[Point (ice hockey)|points]] in the regular season, and is also all-time leader in playoff games coached and game wins. [[Peter Laviolette]] & Brind'Amour are the only coaches to have won the [[Stanley Cup]]<ref name="history"/> with the Hurricanes in the [[2006 Stanley Cup Finals|2006]] & [[2026 Stanley Cup Finals]].<ref name="history"/> None of the Hurricanes coaches have been elected into the [[Hockey Hall of Fame]] as a [[List of members of the Hockey Hall of Fame#Builders|builder]]. Maurice was the head coach of the Hurricanes since the firing of Laviolette, but was replaced by [[Kirk Muller]] on November 28, 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tsn.ca/nhl/story/?id=258260&lid=sublink02&lpos=headlines_main|title=Hurricanes fire Laviolette; make Maurice head coach|publisher=[[CTVglobemedia]]|work=[[The Sports Network]]|date=2008-12-03|accessdate=2008-12-24}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hockey-reference.com/teams/CAR/coaches.html|title=Carolina Hurricanes Coach Register|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|work=Hockey-Reference.com|accessdate=2008-12-21}}</ref> Muller was relieved of coaching duties on May 5, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.canescountry.com/2014/5/5/5683394/coach-kirk-muller-fired-by-carolina-hurricanes | title=Coach Kirk Muller Fired by Carolina Hurricanes | date=5 May 2014 }}</ref> On June 19, 2014, the Hurricanes named [[Bill Peters (ice hockey)|Bill Peters]] their head coach, who decided to opt out of his contract following the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/2014/06/19/3949561/canes-name-detroits-bill-peters.html|title=Canes name Detroit's Bill Peters as new coach|publisher=[[The McClatchy Company]]|work=newsobserver.com|accessdate=2014-11-25|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20141225151738/http://www.newsobserver.com/2014/06/19/3949561/canes-name-detroits-bill-peters.html|archivedate=2014-12-25}}</ref> On May 8, 2018, the Hurricanes named assistant coach and former [[Captain (ice hockey)|team captain]] [[Rod Brind'Amour]] as the head coach for the 2018–19 season.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nhl.com/hurricanes/news/canes-name-rod-brindamour-as-head-coach-298520688|title=Hurricanes Name Rod Brind'Amour as Head Coach|website=NHL.com|language=en-US|access-date=2019-04-07}}</ref>
